input.brief: Ice4Riches : la glace adaptée au verre, produit sculptural et atelier tactile.

direction.name: The object, large
direction.idea: Show the thing, bigger than seems reasonable. One photographed object fills the first screen, scaled until the viewport crops it, with the text small and tucked beside or behind it. The crop is the idea: a record whose edge leaves the top-right corner, a bottle whose shoulder runs off the bottom, a chair seen so close you read its grain. Being that close reads as confidence in the object. Everything else on the page serves it: details as tight close-ups, facts as short lines, one way to buy.
direction.composition: First screen: the object occupies 55–75% of the viewport and breaks at least one edge. It sits on a flat field (ground colour or one bold colour), never in a box. The headline is short and either very large and partly hidden behind the object (10–13vw, the object overlapping two or three letters) or small (28–36px) in the opposite corner with a one-line description. No navigation bar beyond a wordmark and one action. Following sections: a row of three or four close-up details at different crop ratios (not equal tiles), a single wide photograph of the object in use, a plain list of facts set large (materials, size, price) aligned to one edge, then the purchase action. The object returns once at the end from a different angle.
direction.typography: Either very large and structural or very small and precise; pick one for the headline and hold it. Facts are set in the text face at 22–28px, not in a table.
direction.colour: A flat field chosen to make the object's own colour sing (its complement, or a tone darker than its shadow side). One field for the whole page, or a second for the facts section.
direction.imagery: Use the product's own photographs if they exist. Otherwise use a still-life from the dealt set as a stand-in and say so. Prefer images with a plain background; use `mix-blend-mode: multiply` on light fields so a white studio background disappears into the page colour.
direction.photoTreatment: Scale the main image well past its container (`width: 120–160%`) and let `overflow: hidden` on the section do the cropping.
direction.richness: The object's surface at close range, and the tension of the crop.
direction.pitfalls: A small centred product shot with space all round is a catalogue thumbnail, not this direction. If the image has a busy background it cannot sit on a field; crop tighter or change image. Keep text off the object's focal area.

hero.name: Object cropped by three edges
hero.blueprint: A flat off-white or single bold colour field with no navigation bar: only a small wordmark top-right at 24px and the single action fixed bottom-right as a solid rectangular button. The left 60% of the screen is one object photographed on a plain background and scaled far past its container. Set the image to about 150% of the hero's height, rotate it 10 to 20 degrees and position it so the top, left and bottom edges of the viewport all crop it and only its right-hand third is fully inside; use `overflow: hidden` on the section and `mix-blend-mode: multiply` if the field is light. The headline fills the right half: two stacked lines of very bold lowercase at clamp(120px, 13vw, 210px), right-aligned 16px from the right edge, tracking -0.05em, line-height 0.86, vertically centred. It sits behind the object in the stacking order, so the object's right-hand contour tucks over the first one or two letters of each line. One supporting sentence at 18px, max 28ch, is right-aligned under the headline on columns 9–12. Nothing else is on the screen: no second image, no list.
hero.mobile: The object moves to the top: the image is 150vw wide, rotated, cropped by the top, left and right edges, and occupies the upper 52svh. The headline sits below it at 19vw on two lines, right-aligned at a 12px margin, its first line overlapped by the object's lower contour. The supporting sentence follows at 16px, right-aligned. The action button stays fixed bottom-right.
hero.headline: Two lines of one or two short words each, up to about 8 characters per line at 13vw, partly tucked behind the object.

type.note: One neo-grotesk doing everything: semibold headings pulled tight, small regular text, no capitals and no second voice. Suits software, hardware and studio pages that want to look exact and unshowy.

palette.name: Graphite and orange
palette.note: Graphite and cool light-grey sections alternate, graphite taking about two thirds, and photographs are desaturated so nothing competes. Safety orange marks the buttons, one thick solid bar across the top of the page and the highlighted item in a list or chart.

photos.note: hands at work, craft and making
photos.treatment: Scale the main image well past its container (`width: 120–160%`) and let `overflow: hidden` on the section do the cropping.

motion.name: Shutter image
motion.description: The one hero or showcase image opens from an edge with a clip-path over about 1.1 seconds while the picture inside settles from 1.12 scale to rest. Use it once, on the image that matters most; later images simply are there. Recipe: 'Image shutter' in references/motion.md.

sections.name: Two objects, two fields
sections.blueprint: Two panels side by side, each 50vw wide and 92svh tall, in two different flat tones from the palette, meeting on a clean vertical edge with no gap. Each panel is dominated by one cut-out object photograph scaled to 130–150% of the panel's width and positioned so the panel's top edge crops it: the reader sees the lower two-thirds of the object, very close. On light panels use mix-blend-mode: multiply to lose a white studio background. Along the bottom of each panel, 28px in from the edges, one row: the name at 20px medium and a price or fact at 17px on the left; on the right, two small rectangular actions, one filled with ink and one with paper. Nothing sits in the middle of a panel. The heading, two to four words at 32–40px, is set at the top-left of the first panel only, in the empty corner beside the object.
sections.mobile: Panels stack, each 78svh tall, the object scaled to 150% of the width and cut by the top and right edges. The bottom row becomes two lines: name and fact, then the two actions side by side at full width. The heading sits top-left on the first panel at 26px.

sections.name: One verb at a time
sections.blueprint: Three to five full-bleed panels, each 100svh tall, stacked with no gap; each is one stage and holds one photograph covering it. In every panel a single word, the verb for that stage ('Cut', 'Fold', 'Stitch', 'Press'), is set at clamp(96px, 17vw, 300px), heavy and centred, inside a wrapper that is position: sticky; top: 50% and shifted up by half its own height. Because each word is sticky only within its own panel, it holds the centre of the screen while its photograph passes behind it, and is then pushed out by the next panel's verb. Use mix-blend-mode: difference in white, or one solid colour tested on every image. One sentence at 18px sits in the bottom-left corner of each panel over a neutral scrim limited to that corner. There is no separate heading: the verbs, read in order, are both the heading and the sequence.
sections.mobile: Panels stay 100svh, each photograph cropped to a vertical slice. The verb is 24vw, still sticky at the centre. The sentence sits along the bottom over a scrim at 16px, full width with 16px margins.

sections.name: Inset panel, shaped portrait
sections.blueprint: A deep-toned panel inset 20px from the page edges with a 12px radius, about 110svh tall, `overflow: hidden`. Left half: a two-line statement of four to seven words at clamp(40px, 4.4vw, 64px) in a pale ink, top-left with 56px padding; it is the heading and has nothing above it. Below it a photograph of the person or the workshop, masked with `clip-path` or an SVG `mask` to one bold shape taken from the subject (a four-lobed flower, a circle, an arch, a chamfered block), 38vw across, positioned so the panel's bottom edge crops its lowest fifth. Right side, starting at 63% of the width and 56px from the top: two text blocks 300px wide and 64px apart, each a subhead at 22px over a four-line paragraph at 15px; then one solid button in the accent colour. Between the statement and the text blocks the panel is empty. One photograph only.
sections.mobile: The panel is inset 10px and stacks: the statement at 8.5vw, then the two text blocks at full width, the button, and last the shaped photograph at 86vw across, centred and cropped by the panel's bottom edge by a quarter of its height.

sections.name: Visit card on a photograph
sections.blueprint: A full-bleed photograph of the place, 100vw by 100svh, carries one solid card and nothing else. The card is a filled panel in the paper colour, fully opaque, 380px wide with 8px corners and 32px padding, placed in the upper-right corner 60px from the top and right edges (or the upper-left: pick the corner where the photograph is calmest). It holds, top to bottom: a two- or three-word title at 28px in a light weight; the address on two lines at 16px; the opening hours as three rows with days at the left and times right-aligned in tabular figures; the phone number; then, flush with the card's bottom edge and spanning its width, a solid booking button 52px tall. The card may be `position: sticky; top: 60px` inside a taller section so it holds while the photograph scrolls beneath it. The photograph's focal point must stay clear of the card. No heading outside the card.
sections.mobile: The photograph is 100vw by 70svh. The card leaves the corner: it spans the width with 16px margins and overlaps the photograph's bottom edge by 80px, so image and card interlock. The booking button is full width, 56px tall, at the card's bottom.

sections.name: The back of the card
sections.blueprint: The footer is the reverse side of the page's artefact, laid out as the back of a postcard. A paper-coloured panel spans columns 2–11 on the contrasting ground, about 420px tall, its top edge cut into a row of twelve semicircular scallops (an inline SVG path or `clip-path`, each scallop about 100px wide). The panel is divided by space into two halves. Left half: a short sign-off of two to four words at 32px, then two or three lines at 16px, written like a message. Right half: the address block, four left-aligned lines at 18px with 12px between them, each line a link (email, telephone, street, social); above it in the top-right corner, a stamp: one small photograph, 3:4 and 88px wide, with a 6px paper-coloured margin. Along the panel's bottom edge, a single centred line at 12px gives the copyright like a printer's imprint.
sections.mobile: The panel runs full width with six scallops across its top edge. The stamp sits top-right at 64px wide; the sign-off and message come first, then the address lines at 17px beneath them, then the imprint line centred at 12px.

references.name: The Watch
references.idea: A single 3D watch is the only actor: it holds centre stage and turns, flips and finally explodes into parts while giant product-name letters slide behind and in front of it.
references.hero: Light grey field with soft darker blurs toward the corners. A steel chronograph rendered in 3D stands upright at dead centre, about 80% of viewport height. Behind it the product name is set once across the full width in a wide, squared geometric sans at 24vw in mid-grey; the watch covers the middle character, so only two letters at the left edge and two at the right are readable. A thin circle about 700px across with faint radial spokes and one darker arc sits behind the watch like a dial diagram. No navigation, logo, body copy or button anywhere.
references.type: Nekst, a wide squared geometric sans, regular weight, uppercase, used only huge (up to 25vw) in black, mid-grey and white within one line stack. Body is Inter at 12px in 130px columns, roughly a 30x jump with nothing in between.
references.colour: #e8e8e8 #c7c7c7 #a1a1a1 #6b6b6b #0a0a0a #ffffff — Entirely greyscale: pale grey ground with out-of-focus darker clouds, type in black, grey and white. The page darkens to mid-grey for the exploded view. Only the brass gear train adds warmth.
references.imagery: One real-time 3D steel watch shown front, three-quarter, caseback and exploded into dial, movement and plates lined up on a horizontal axis. No photographs; the object floats with no ground shadow.
references.layout: No grid chrome at all: the object holds the centre while type moves around it. Giant letters crop at any edge, captions sit in a 130px column left or right of the watch, and one product label is rotated 90 degrees.

sections.description: Four stacked lines of uppercase display type about 110px tall, flush left at mid-page and running off the right edge: line one mid-grey, line two black, lines three and four pale grey to white. The watch, tilted three-quarter, floats over the upper right of the stack and hides parts of letters, so type and object share the same space instead of sitting side by side.

The watch is turned to show its open caseback, placed just left of centre. To its right, a 130px-wide column holds two micro-paragraphs at 12px, each with a grey one-line title above. A small grey circular toggle sits far left. A white display word crops off the top edge. The rest of the frame is empty grey with a darker blurred cloud at upper right.

Exploded view. The ground shifts to a mid-grey vertical gradient with a faint horizon line. The watch's components (dial, tourbillon, movement, barrel, bridges) are separated and spaced along one horizontal axis at eye level like specimens. Tiny part names are set vertically along the bottom edge under each piece; a small prompt with a plus icon sits top-centre.

steal: Set the product name so large that the product itself replaces one of its characters, leaving the name half-hidden and the object as the missing letter.
Stack one display line in three tints (black, mid-grey, white) on a grey ground so a single typeface produces depth without colour.
End a product story with an exploded view laid out on one horizontal axis with vertical micro-labels instead of a spec table.
references.media: One fixed full-bleed WebGL canvas renders every picture: a steel chronograph about 620px tall (69% of the height, 29% of the width) centred inside a 720px ring with the giant model code behind it, then the watch from every side, an exploded line of parts on an axis with leader labels, particle ribbons on black, a black-finish reprise and a close-up cropped by the bottom edge. No photographs and no video; two very tall gradient overlays hand the ground from light to dark and back.
references.motion: The preloader holds at least 4.5s on the 3D assets, then its 720px circle stays to become the ring round the watch while a dark arc draws clockwise over 1.2s. Lenis drives one pinned, scrubbed timeline over 38 screens: the watch turns, separates into parts, the ground moves from #ebebeb to #a1a1a1 to #0a0a0a, and headline lines change colour by their distance from the viewport centre; per-character transforms are written every frame, smoothed by a 20ms ease-out.

references.name: ARCHIV
references.idea: A waitlist page as a museum plinth: one cut-out everyday object at a time, centred on off-white beneath a heavy serif wordmark.
references.hero: Off-white single screen with no scroll. A heavy high-contrast serif wordmark in black caps sits top-left at a 56px margin, about 410px wide (28% of the viewport) and 80px tall. Opposite, top-right at the same margin, one line of 14px sans description aligns with the wordmark's top. Dead centre, one photographed object (a painted wooden pepper mill about 140px wide and 440px tall) stands on a barely visible lighter rounded square with a soft contact shadow; other objects replace it in turn. Below, a centred 11px grey line, then a white rounded email field 236px wide with a circled arrow inside its right end. Roughly 80% is empty.
references.type: The wordmark is drawn lettering in a heavy display serif with tight spacing, cap height about 5.5vw. All live text is Helvetica Neue regular at 14px and about 11px, black or grey. Two text sizes only; the contrast is wordmark against near-invisible interface text.
references.colour: #f1efec #000000 #ffffff #d9261c #e8a317 #7a7a75 — Warm off-white field, black wordmark, a white input; all colour arrives through whichever object is showing (red and yellow mill, tan leather, blue cap).
references.imagery: Studio cut-outs of single everyday objects in three-quarter view with a soft grounded shadow on matching off-white, each scaled to similar visual mass and centred, one at a time, no frame.
references.layout: One fixed viewport with four elements: wordmark top-left, description top-right, object in the exact centre, form bottom-centre. Margins of 56px, no rules, nav or footer. On mobile the wordmark centres and the description disappears.

sections.description: The central object rotates through unrelated things (pepper mill, sling chair, sticker-covered hydrant, layered iced drink, record player, baseball cap), each photographed in the same light and replaced in place within a zone roughly 250-300px square. Shadow direction and visual weight stay constant, so the object is the page's only variable and no carousel controls are needed.

Beneath the object, a centred line of 11px grey text, a 30px gap, then a white field about 236 by 52px with 12px radius: light grey placeholder at left and a 26px circle-outlined arrow as the submit control inside the right end. No button label, border or shadow; the field is the only pure white on the page, which marks it as the one interactive thing.

steal: Build a pre-launch page from four elements only (wordmark top-left, one-line description top-right, a single centred object, an email field) and leave the rest of the screen empty.
Cycle one consistently lit cut-out object in the same spot to show range without adding a grid or carousel controls.
Make the email field the only pure-white element on an off-white page, with submit as a circled arrow inside it rather than a labelled button.

references.name: Vero New-York
references.idea: Treat a keepsake like couture: a slow close-up film opens, then a white 3D sculpture of a dress stays pinned at centre while one sentence in mixed capitals and italics passes over it.
references.hero: Full-bleed video with no scrim: an extreme close-up of a woman's profile against a burnt-orange wall, a blurred pale sculpture occupying the right 40% of the frame in the foreground. Exactly at centre sits the four-letter wordmark in white serif capitals, about 240px wide; 25px beneath it a one-line tagline at 20px alternates italic lowercase connectives with roman capitals. Two translucent frosted rectangles with square corners float 30px from the top corners: a 130px menu button left, a 250px commission button right, both in small capitals. A tiny chevron marks the bottom centre. Nothing else; the image carries the screen.
references.type: Louize Display at 120px (8.3vw), centred: nouns in roman capitals, connective words in lowercase italic at the same size within the same line. Beausite Classic grotesk appears only for a bold 17px lead and footer links. Serif body runs 11–16px; the footer wordmark fills the width.
references.colour: #f3f0ed #181615 #b4521f #c6a788 #ffffff #97775a — Burnt orange and skin tones in the opening film, then warm off-white pages with near-black type and a plaster-white sculpture; orange returns only inside one small photograph.
references.imagery: Shallow-focus warm video up top; a real-time 3D plaster-white bust and lace dress on off-white, cropped at neck and hem and fading into the page; one small square-cornered photo of the dress on a plinth against orange.
references.layout: Everything sits on one centre axis with wide empty flanks. Two fixed corner buttons persist as soft-shadowed white tiles. Headlines take two lines each and share the screen with the pinned 3D object; body text is confined to a 240px centred column.

sections.description: Off-white screen. The sentence is delivered in halves: first two centred lines at 8.3vw in the upper third, with a small diamond glyph beside the italic word, while a white 3D bust rises from the bottom centre at about 30% of the width. Scrolling turns the sculpture to show the laced back, now filling the full height of the centre column, and the second half of the sentence lands over the skirt in the lower third.

The skirt's hem dissolves into the off-white at the top of the screen. Beneath it is a centred text stack only about 240px wide: a three-line lead in bold grotesk at 17px, four lines of serif body at 11px, and a small white rectangular button with a diffuse shadow carrying the same italic-plus-capitals label as the header button. The lower half of the viewport is left empty.

A tiny centred eyebrow in the italic-plus-capitals style, then a two-line headline at about 8vw where each line begins with a lowercase italic word and ends in capitals, the lines offset so the block reads as a stagger. Under it, centred, one small photo about 330×290px with square corners: saturated orange backdrop, white dress on a plinth. The image is deliberately much smaller than the type.

Off-white. Top-left, a five-item vertical link list in small grotesk; under it a newsletter field drawn as a single underline with an arrow; three social links right-aligned at the same level. Then the wordmark in near-black serif capitals stretches across the full width, about 45% of the viewport tall. A final row of tiny grey legal links sits beneath.

steal: Within one serif headline, set the nouns in roman capitals and the small connective words in lowercase italic at the same size.
Pin a single white 3D object on an off-white page and deliver one sentence in two halves over its front and back as it turns.
Follow a huge two-line headline with one deliberately small, saturated photograph centred beneath it instead of a full-width image.
references.media: A full-bleed 10s studio film covers the whole first screen with no scrim, the wordmark centred on it. Then a fixed render of the dress sculpture that the camera travels down while headlines rise over it, an inset window under a headline that grows to full bleed, a pinned full-bleed stepper with right-to-left wipes, a sticky picture beside parallax pictures, a grid of 4:5 thumbnails in columns at different speeds, and a 3D coin passing through a typographic wall; 0px corners and two strict photo families, brides on burnt orange and white resin on grey.
references.motion: A preloader of about 3.5-4s: a centred serif statement with a small photo window between its lines that opens by clip-path into the hero film over 1.4s cubic-bezier(.83,0,.17,1), then the wordmark fades in. Native scroll driven by script: the beige page slides up over the fixed hero, a 3840px sticky stepper advances three photographs, and headline words rise out of line masks over 1.2-1.4s cubic-bezier(.19,1,.22,1) at 0.1s steps; images clip in over 1.6s cubic-bezier(.22,1,.36,1).
